sbsistemas.what: I solidified my professional foundation in front-end development, building applications focused on usability, maintainability, type safety, reusable components and sound engineering practices.

luizalabs.what: At Luizalabs, Magalu's technology unit, I worked on web and mobile apps for physical store operations and on the services behind them, with a Go back end on GCP, at a nationwide retailer operating at high scale.
impact: Developed solutions used in inventory and logistics operations across 1,000+ stores
Contributed to corporate apps in the daily workflow of 1,000+ stock clerks
Services in Go and Node.js on GCP, communicating through RabbitMQ queues, plus REST APIs and micro frontends in React and React Native
Code and operations tracked in SonarQube and Grafana
Lived through Black Fridays from the inside: the week a retail system can't fail

lemon.period: July 2026 - present · AI team, inside Finance
lemon.what: On Lemon's AI team, I work from inside a business area: I'm part of the day-to-day Finance operation, I find the manual work and I decide what becomes a product. Since August, I've put six internal products into production, from the UI to the database and the AWS infrastructure.
impact: Six finance products in three months: bank reconciliation, payment batches, suppliers, invoices and debit notes
Each one end to end: React front end, Fastify API with PostgreSQL and infrastructure as code with Pulumi
On AWS: containers on ECS Fargate, database on Aurora (RDS), events with EventBridge and SQS, secrets in Secrets Manager, delivery through API Gateway and CloudFront
A fast delivery pace, with AI agents in the loop and critical review before anything goes live

klick.name: Klick
klick.tagline: An offline-first speedcubing timer for all 13 WCA events.
klick.heroAlt: The Klick timer on desktop, with the scramble and session averages

pain.title: The history that vanished.
pain.body: In the research before Klick v2, the story that came up most was from people who had lost anywhere from months to three years of times: cleared browser data, a new phone, an app that didn't save them properly.
pain.caption: paraphrased from real accounts on cubing forums, gathered for the Klick v2 research

decisions.title: What came first.
items: Times live on the device (IndexedDB) and the app works offline after the first visit.
Automatic local backups every 50 solves and once a day, with a 30-day trash bin.
An optional, passwordless account (email code or passkey) to sync and keep cloud copies.
All 13 WCA events with official scrambles, and csTimer import for anyone switching from it.

grimory.name: Grimory
grimory.tagline: A D&D 5e table in Portuguese, from character to session.
grimory.heroAlt: The Grimory compendium open to the Longsword entry

pain.title: The character sheet, mid-session.
pain.body: Players open their sheet on their phone mid-game: one hand, quick glances, numbers to roll and rules to check without leaving the sheet. The DM runs combat from a laptop.

decisions.title: The AI proposes, the rules decide.
items: Describe a concept and the AI proposes a complete sheet, with its choices explained, that opens in the builder for review.
The rules engine validates everything: an invalid option never shows up.
Each table picks the 2014 or 2024 rules, and every screen respects that choice.
Only content that can be distributed: SRD 5.1 and 5.2 under CC-BY-4.0, with the source cited on every rule.

product.title: In use at my group's table.
product.body: A sheet that knows the rules, a translated compendium with the table's homebrew, a session journal and the Chama-guia, the familiar that gives the AI a face.
